about: Every Docker object, operation and spec element in reference/upstream (see SOURCES.md) with its decided Terraform name (DECISIONS.md). status is computed from internal/provider/registry_gen.go and the STUB(pass5) / PARTIAL(pass5) markers in internal/provider. Paths in sources are relative to reference/.

naming_questions.question: NetworkConnect/NetworkDisconnect: add a standalone `docker_network_attachment` resource (container x network pair), or make docker_container `networks` connect/disconnect in place instead of forcing replacement? (or both, with a conflict warning)
Build cache prune action name: `docker_builder_prune` (matches `docker builder prune`) or `docker_build_cache_prune` (avoids confusion with docker_buildx_builder)?
Standalone build: add an action `docker_image_build`, or keep builds only in docker_image's `build` block? If added, is the name too close to docker_image?

Managing an already-joined swarm node (labels/availability/role via NodeUpdate) that Terraform did not join: extend docker_swarm_node with an adopt mode, or add a separate `docker_node` resource (name matches existing data.docker_node)?
Node role actions: `docker_node_promote` / `docker_node_demote` (CLI words, matching docker_node_drain/activate) or one `docker_node_role` action with role = manager|worker?
Logs: separate `docker_service_logs` and `docker_task_logs` data sources, or extend data.docker_logs with service_id / task_id arguments?
SystemAuth (/auth) returns an identity token: model as an ephemeral resource (e.g. `docker_registry_login`) next to ephemeral docker_registry_token, or skip it?
PluginCreate: action `docker_plugin_create` (one-shot) or a resource (it has PluginDelete) with a different name to avoid confusion with docker_plugin (install from registry)?
Container one-off read of files: data source `docker_container_file` (GET archive) vs an action; and copy-in at any time: action `docker_container_upload` or `docker_container_cp`?

Swarm rotation actions: separate `docker_swarm_rotate_unlock_key` and `docker_swarm_ca_rotate`, or one `docker_swarm_rotate` action with what = worker_token|manager_token|unlock_key|ca (absorbing docker_swarm_rotate_tokens)?
Imperative compose actions beside the docker_compose resource: name them docker_compose_up/down (CLI-shaped), docker_compose_apply/destroy, or skip up/down since the resource covers them?

`compose config` render: data source docker_compose_config (visually collides with docker_config and top-level `configs`), docker_compose_project / docker_compose_model, or a provider function compose_render?
`compose ps` / `compose ls`: docker_compose_ps + docker_compose_ls (CLI names) or docker_compose_containers + docker_compose_projects (noun convention like docker_containers)?
`compose volumes`: add a docker_compose_volumes data source, or document data.docker_volume/list.docker_volume with a project label filter (avoids the docker_volume clash)?
Per-container verbs (start/stop/restart/kill/pause/unpause): separate docker_compose_* actions, or one set of docker_container_* actions with an optional project/service selector?
`compose scale` vs existing docker_service_scale: new docker_compose_scale action, or extend docker_service_scale to compose local projects?
Compose top-level elements: keep all inside docker_compose, or split docker_compose_service/network/volume (confusable with docker_service/docker_network/docker_volume)?
jobs: support in docker_compose (run once on apply) plus docker_compose_run for manual triggers, or leave unsupported but add a warning?

Manifest lists: `docker_registry_manifest_list` (proposed, registry family) vs `docker_manifest_list` vs `docker_buildx_imagetools`? One resource for both `docker manifest create/push` and `buildx imagetools create`.
BuildKit build: keep extending `docker_image` (build block) vs add `docker_buildx_build`? Proposed: extend docker_image, and add action `docker_buildx_bake` for multi-target / non-image outputs.

Stack: keep existing `docker_stack` vs a `docker_swarm_stack` prefix for consistency with docker_swarm_*? Proposed: keep docker_stack; new stack data sources `docker_stacks` and `docker_stack` (or `docker_stack_services`).

Context: skip `docker_context` (provider `context`/`host` arguments already select the daemon) vs a read-only `docker_context` data source that resolves a context's endpoint/TLS from ~/.docker? Proposed: skip.
Build cache prune: one action for both daemon build cache (POST /build/prune, Z1) and buildx builders (BuildKit gRPC): `docker_buildx_prune` vs `docker_build_cache_prune` vs `docker_builder_prune`?

Buildx builder data sources: `docker_buildx_builder` (singular, same name as the resource) + `docker_buildx_builders`; buildx history as `docker_buildx_history` (+ `docker_buildx_history_record`) or one data source with an optional ref?
docker buildx stop: action `docker_buildx_builder_stop` or skip (low value)?
Disk usage: `docker_buildx_disk_usage` separate from Z1's system df data source, or one data source with an optional builder?

Shape: (a) one type per instruction (docker_dockerfile_run, docker_dockerfile_from, ...) vs (b) a single data source data.docker_dockerfile with ordered nested blocks (stage { from, run, copy ... }) rendering Dockerfile text vs (c) a provider function. (b) recommended: ordering and stages fit nested blocks; 21 trivial types would bloat the registry.
Directives: docker_dockerfile_directive_syntax/escape/check types vs top-level attributes syntax, escape, check { skip = [...], error = bool } on data.docker_dockerfile (recommended).
Include MAINTAINER (deprecated) at all, or omit and steer users to LABEL org.opencontainers.image.authors?
ONBUILD: separate block nesting an instruction vs an `onbuild = true` attribute on each instruction block?
Stages: model FROM ... AS name as a `stage` block with `name` (recommended) rather than a FROM flag?
check rule names: validate against a pinned list (21 rules at frontend 1.28) or accept free strings?

Raw outputs that are not JSON: container logs `logs` (vs `logs_text`), exec `output` (vs `stdout`+`stderr`), image-build `build_log`, container-file `content_base64` (vs `content`). SCHEMA lists raw names as fixed or `<thing>_json`; which form for non-JSON streams?

Hash name when an item has two raw outputs (container-file stat_json + content_base64): used `<raw>_sha256` (`stat_json_sha256`, `content_base64_sha256`) per SCHEMA; confirm, or should file content keep `content_sha256`?

Action result output: `result` (whole API JSON body, structured) vs flattening each field (`space_reclaimed`, `exit_code`) to top-level outputs. Used `result` + identity lists of deleted IDs; container state-change actions use `state` (ContainerState).
List data sources: identity as `ids` / `names` list(string) vs per-element identity inside the structured list only.
Files written by actions (export, save, upload): sha256 exposed as identity `archive_sha256` because category hash requires a raw string output; or should these get a hash category exception?
docker_swarm_init exposes the cluster ID today as `cluster_id`; the contract uses `id` = ClusterInfo.ID. Keep `cluster_id` as an alias, or drop it?
Plural data sources: structured list named after the type (`services`, `nodes`, ...) with raw `<plural>_json` (this lane), or a uniform `items` / `items_json` across every plural data source?
Action identity for the target: `node_id` / `service_id` (this lane) or plain `id` like resources?
docker_compose exposes the project name as `id` and `project_name`; the contract's identity name is `name`. Add a `name` alias, rename project_name to name (breaking), or keep project_name?

Facets of docker_compose: one `project` attribute (whole project) as proposed, or per-slice attributes (`project_services`, `project_networks`, ...) that do not clash with today's computed `services`/`networks`/`volumes` ID maps?
Action results: `result` object {exit_code, stdout, stderr} (as proposed for docker_compose_exec / _run) or flat `exit_code` / `stdout` / `stderr` like docker_exec_output?

docker_image and data.docker_image expose `repo_digest`; the contract name is `image_digest_ref`: rename (breaking), add `image_digest_ref` and deprecate `repo_digest`, or keep `repo_digest` as the contract name?

data.docker_registry_image exposes `sha256_digest` (= contract `digest`) and `id` = `<name>@<digest>` (≈ `image_digest_ref`): add `digest` + `image_digest_ref` and deprecate `sha256_digest`, or keep the current names?
`image_id` duplicates `id` on docker_image and data.docker_image: keep both, or deprecate `image_id`?
data.docker_dockerfile: expose the original input text as a second raw output (`source_dockerfile` + `source_dockerfile_sha256`) beside the re-rendered `dockerfile`, or only the rendered form?
Structured output name on each dockerfile_block item: the lowercase keyword (`run`, `copy`, `from`, current) or one uniform name (`block`)?
data.docker_dockerfile image mode: name the provenance outputs `reconstructed` + `fidelity` (current, both identity) or a single `fidelity` (`exact`/`approximate`)?
docker_stack data source structured output: `services` + `tasks` (current) or split tasks into docker_tasks only and drop `tasks` here?

stack ls Services count: `services` in docker_stacks (upstream name) while docker_stack.stack.services is the compose service map; rename the docker_stacks field to `services_count`, or keep upstream `services`?

Schema extension: swagger source entries carry `primary: true` on the one item that is the operation's home; other items that also use the op list it without `primary` (e.g. ContainerInspect in docker_container resource vs data source, SwarmUpdate in rotate actions). Swagger sources also carry `min_api` where the CHANGELOG states the endpoint was added.

min_api: the swagger descriptions carry no version text (only Session's deprecation). D: One new item: dockerfile:data-dockerfile (data.docker_dockerfile). Confirmed missing: no docker_dockerfile type in internal/provider (register_*.go); docker_image only takes a Dockerfile path.
ImageHistory and ImageInspect are cited without primary: their primary homes are engine:image-history and engine:image-data.

Image mode reads ImageHistory (#/definitions/ImageHistoryResponseItem, CreatedBy) and ImageInspect (#/definitions/ImageInspect Config); the result is approximate. Image mode cannot recover a Dockerfile. It rebuilds an approximate single-stage instruction list from the image history (ImageHistoryResponseItem.CreatedBy, newest first, reversed) plus ImageConfig for the final CMD/ENTRYPOINT/ENV/EXPOSE/USER/WORKDIR/LABEL/HEALTHCHECK/SHELL/STOPSIGNAL/VOLUME values, so fidelity = approximate: FROM and earlier stages are lost (base-image layers appear as leading history entries), COPY/ADD sources are only content hashes, RUN --mount/--network/--security flags and heredoc structure are not recorded, and images built by other tools may have empty or squashed history. History CreatedBy records build-arg values, so image-mode stages/history/dockerfile are sensitive.
Matches option (b) of z4's first naming question (one data.docker_dockerfile with ordered nested blocks).

Pass 5 Lane D/Z: the `git` source became `url` (a raw HTTPS fetch of one file, pure Go, 4 MiB cap, no git); `git_commit` stays in the schema and is always null. Builder mode (`stage` blocks) is a fifth source (`source_type` = blocks). Instruction order across keywords is one ordered `instruction` block per stage holding exactly one keyword block. The per-keyword structured objects stay JSON strings until their fields are mapped completely (fields_complete). Block-level outputs (instruction, stage_index, instruction_index, dockerfile, content_sha256, dockerfile_syntax) sit on each instruction / global_arg block; the `stage` block has no computed `instruction` (it would clash with the nested block), its FROM data is in stages[*].

outputs:A: Scope: every layer=engine item except engine:image, engine:image-data, engine:registry-image-data (Lane D). Field names come mechanically from swagger.yaml (API 1.56) via $ref/allOf resolution; every pointer was checked to resolve.

fields depth: top-level fields plus one nested level for every object-valued field (MAXDEPTH=2). fields_complete is false wherever a second-level field is itself an object/list of objects/map of objects left to the mechanical rule.

Field pointers: a property whose schema is a $ref points at the referenced definition (as in SCHEMA.md's example); every other property points at #/.../properties/<Name>. allOf components are flattened (HostConfig = Resources + its own properties; NetworkInspect = Network + Containers/Services/Status).

snake_case: CamelCase split with IPv4/IPv6/IOps/IDs kept whole (EnableIPv6 -> enable_ipv6, BlkioDeviceReadIOps -> blkio_device_read_iops); names already lower_snake (ContainerStatsResponse, ImageSearch, OCIDescriptor) are kept; linkTarget -> link_target.

known_after_apply: resources true for everything computed by create (id, inspect, digests, version outputs since they are recorded at create); inputs echoed back (registry-image name/image_ref, tag image_ref) false. Data sources false (they read at plan time unless their inputs are unknown). Actions: true for everything, since the values only exist when the action is invoked.

Actions: Terraform actions cannot return values today, so every action item is outputs_status=missing; the outputs list what the action reads back (identity, the API's JSON result as a structured `result`/`state`, version). Action items carry no raw output except exec `output` and image-build `build_log`.

Version outputs: both engine_api_version and docker_server_version on every item, sourced from #/definitions/SystemVersion (ApiVersion, Version); engine_api_version is the negotiated value, not the daemon maximum.

Sensitive (whole raw+structured pair): container inspect (Config.Env), volume inspect / volume list (driver Options can carry CIFS/NFS passwords), plugin inspect / list (Settings.Env), image history (CreatedBy shows build-arg values), image attestations (provenance records build args), registry auth (IdentityToken), plus logs, exec output, build_log and container file content.

Not marked sensitive: container top / containers list (command lines can carry secrets but are not the env/secret channel), image inspect for docker_tag (Config.Env is image-baked; align with Lane D's choice for docker_image), info (daemon masks proxy credentials).

provided: computed by matching output names against attribute names in the item's provider file(s); only identity outputs (id, name, labels, digest, mountpoint...) exist today, no raw/structured/version/hash output exists anywhere in the provider.
outputs:B: Lane B owns layer=swarm items only. docker_stack / docker_stacks / stack services are layer cli-only in inventory.json (cli-only:stack, cli-only:stack-services, cli-only:stacks), so stack_yaml / compose_spec_version are not in this file; the lane that owns cli-only should add them.

Structured outputs are named `inspect` (single object; raw `inspect_json` serializes it) or the plural type name for list data sources (`services` + `services_json`). Address example: docker_service.x.inspect.spec.task_template.container_spec.image.

fields were generated mechanically from swagger.yaml (API 1.56) by following $ref / allOf / items / additionalProperties to the leaves, so every upstream name is a real property; fields_complete true means the whole tree is listed. Snake_case keeps acronym runs together (NanoCPUs -> nano_cpus, SELinuxContext -> selinux_context, ExternalCAs -> external_cas, VirtualIPs -> virtual_ips, TLSInfo -> tls_info).
Objects with neither properties nor additionalProperties in the swagger are tf_type dynamic (e.g. ServiceSpec.Mode.Global, GlobalJob).
version_index (swarm object Version.Index) is identity, never the version category; version outputs are only engine_api_version / docker_server_version from GET /version (SystemVersion).
known_after_apply: resources and actions true (computed by create / invoke); data sources false (they read existing objects; unknown only when an argument comes from an unapplied resource).

Sensitive: service/task inspect and lists (ContainerSpec.Env/Args/Command), join tokens, unlock key, logs. Secret inspect is not sensitive because the Engine never returns SecretSpec.Data. The swarm inspect excludes JoinTokens (separate sensitive join_tokens) and relies on the daemon redacting Spec.CAConfig.SigningCAKey (swarmkit redacts it on GetCluster; the swagger still lists the field) - unverified against a live daemon.
Hash outputs (content_sha256) are not sensitive even when their raw output is: a SHA-256 does not reveal the value.
outputs:C: compose:name carries the whole-project raw/structured outputs (compose_yaml, project, content_sha256) because it is the facet that IS the project (its name/id); compose:cli-config (docker_compose_config) repeats them for the read-only render. Every other docker_compose facet (services, networks, volumes, configs, secrets, models, jobs, include) declares the SAME `project` attribute restricted to its slice, plus no_raw_reason pointing at compose:name.

Pointers: both schema files use JSON Schema 2020-12 `$defs`, not `definitions`; pointers are written `#/$defs/...` (e.g. #/$defs/container_spec/properties/image). A service's direct properties are the union of $defs/container_spec, $defs/workload_spec and $defs/service (allOf); each field points at the def that declares it. Field pointers are into compose-spec.json; the same JSON path exists in compose-go-embedded.json for every field except jobs.*.extends.

Schema differences (compose-spec @ 3a4a699 vs compose-go v2.16.2 embedded): (1) container_spec mem_limit, memswap_limit, shm_size are integer|string in compose-spec and number|string in compose-go. Those fields carry schema=compose-go-embedded (the provider validates with compose-go); the TF type is number either way after normalization (bytes). build.shm_size is integer|string in BOTH files and is not affected. (2) jobs.*.extends exists only in compose-spec; the field carries schema=compose-spec and the compose:jobs project slice follows compose-spec (output schema=compose-spec), all other project outputs (compose:name, compose:cli-config, every other facet, build, deploy) follow compose-go-embedded.

Normalized-form typing: the structured fields mirror the NORMALIZED project (what `docker compose config` prints), so oneOf short/long forms are typed by their long form: list_or_dict -> map(string) (environment, labels, annotations, sysctls, build.args), string_or_list/command -> list(string), build/extends/include/ports/volumes/secrets/configs entries -> object, depends_on/service networks/service models -> map(object), ulimits -> map(object{soft,hard}), extra_hosts -> map(list(string)), boolean|string -> bool, integer/number|string -> number, external (bool|string|object) -> bool, umask -> string.

Depth: `project` lists every top-level property (version, name, include, services, models, networks, volumes, secrets, configs, jobs); every direct property of a service (and of a job); build, deploy, healthcheck, ports and volumes (long syntax) one more level, and the direct properties of network/volume/secret/config/model/include definitions. Deeper levels (deploy.resources.*, deploy.placement.*, volumes[].bind.*, blkio_config.*, develop.watch[] ...) are left to the mechanical rule: fields_complete=false.

Sensitivity: compose_yaml and project are sensitive as a whole, because environment, env_file, build.args/secrets/ssh, configs.content, secrets sources and ANY interpolated ${VAR} can carry a secret. Fields that are the usual carriers have an extra field-level `sensitive: true` annotation (informational). content_sha256 of a sensitive raw is not marked sensitive. Logs (logs_json/entries), top (process args), ps (Command) and exec/run stdout/stderr are sensitive; this is stricter than today's data.docker_logs (not sensitive) and matches docker_exec_output (sensitive).

Actions: there is no raw/structured requirement; `result`/`results` objects (exec, run, wait) are structured with fields, everything else is identity (IDs/refs changed or returned). known_after_apply is true for every action output.

known_after_apply: compose_yaml/project/hash/image_refs are false because docker_compose parses the project at plan time (spec_hash is computed in plan); IDs created by the Engine are true. Version pins (compose_spec_version, compose_go_version) are build-time constants (false); engine versions are true on resources/actions and false on data sources.
Field annotations beyond SCHEMA.md: `schema`, `schema_note`, `sensitive`, `note` on FIELD and `schema` on OUTPUT, as the lane brief asked; merge.py does not check FIELD keys.

compose:service-build and compose:service-deploy are proposed under docker_image / docker_service (inventory names); their outputs here are only the compose-facing slice (`build`, `deploy` objects + identity), not those resources' Engine inspect outputs, which other lanes own.

compose:cli-ls fields (Name, Status, ConfigFiles) come from `docker compose ls --format json`; compose_ls.md documents the json format but not the keys, so the keys are from compose's output and pointed at the labels they derive from.
outputs:D: Outputs for the 21 dockerfile_block items, engine:image (docker_image), engine:image-data, engine:registry-image-data and the new dockerfile:data-dockerfile.

Every Dockerfile flag is a typed field checked against reference.md (frontend 1.29.0); min_syntax only where reference.md states a 'Minimum Dockerfile version' or 'since Dockerfile v1.x'. ADD has no --from and no heredoc in reference.md, so none is modelled. Heredocs carry no min_syntax (none stated).
Block identity = instruction keyword + stage_index + instruction_index (directives: the directive name, which is file-level and unique). No allowed_violations needed.
Each block also has a raw `dockerfile` (the block rendered) + content_sha256, so a consumer can hand off one instruction as text.

Field-level extra keys: min_syntax, anchor (doc anchor), options (documented values), sensitive (per field), see (item id whose shape a nested object takes), filled_by (local/registry/image), existing_attribute on outputs (today's attribute carrying the same value under another name).

Sensitive: ENV values and ARG defaults (dockerfile:ENV, dockerfile:ARG, and every whole-file dockerfile/stages/global_args output), ImageConfig.Env (config, inspect, inspect_json of docker_image and data.docker_image), image history CreatedBy (build-arg values, per reference.md ARG warning).

Not sensitive by decision: RUN --mount=type=secret. The Dockerfile carries only the secret id, target and env-var name, never the value; values live only in docker_image build.secrets, read at build and never stored. Flip dockerfile:RUN run/dockerfile to sensitive if secret ids must be hidden too.

data.docker_image and data.docker_registry_image share identity (id, name, image_ref, image_digest_ref, digest, platforms, labels, created), structured (manifests, config, inspect) and version outputs; inspect/inspect_json mirror each side's own upstream model (ImageInspect vs DistributionInspect). labels, created, config and manifests[].digest/media_type/size/available are local-only (filled_by).

Image-mode fidelity: Image mode cannot recover a Dockerfile. It rebuilds an approximate single-stage instruction list from the image history (ImageHistoryResponseItem.CreatedBy, newest first, reversed) plus ImageConfig for the final CMD/ENTRYPOINT/ENV/EXPOSE/USER/WORKDIR/LABEL/HEALTHCHECK/SHELL/STOPSIGNAL/VOLUME values, so fidelity = approximate: FROM and earlier stages are lost (base-image layers appear as leading history entries), COPY/ADD sources are only content hashes, RUN --mount/--network/--security flags and heredoc structure are not recorded, and images built by other tools may have empty or squashed history. History CreatedBy records build-arg values, so image-mode stages/history/dockerfile are sensitive.
No OCI image-spec file is harvested under reference/upstream, so the history path is cited via swagger ImageHistoryResponseItem (x-go-name HistoryResponseItem) only.
outputs:E: Lane E owns the 16 non-skipped items with layer buildx or cli-only, including the three docker_stack items (cli-only:stack, cli-only:stack-services, cli-only:stacks; coordinator assignment). cli-only:context, cli-only:login, cli-only:stack-config, cli-only:stack-ps and buildx:version are kind skip, so they get no outputs (contexts' TLSMaterial and login auth are therefore not covered here).
buildx_version is the SOURCES.md pin (buildx v0.38.2) of the buildx semantics a type mirrors; the provider never runs buildx, so it is static, not discovered at runtime.

Builder field names: `docker buildx ls --format` documents .Name/.DriverEndpoint/.LastActivity/.Status/.Buildkit/.Platforms/.Error/.Builder (and .Builder.Name, .Builder.Nodes, node .Name/.Endpoint). The other builder/node fields (Driver Options, Flags, Labels, GC Policy) are recorded with their `docker buildx inspect` text label (`label`), because the harvested docs do not show their JSON keys.
FIELD entries carry `format_field` (Go template placeholder), `label` (pretty/text label), `pointer` (swagger) or `anchor` (doc) as their upstream locator.
docker_registry_image_manifests is the target of two items (buildx:imagetools-inspect, cli-only:manifest-inspect); both get the identical output list.
buildx:stop status is category structured with a one-field list so the action has a typed result; actions have no V2 requirement.

cli-only:stack `stack` follows compose-spec #/$defs/service (allOf service + container_spec + workload_spec, 94 top-level keys); nested compose objects (deploy, build, healthcheck, networks, ...) are dynamic under the mechanical rule.
outputs:P5: Pass 5 Lane 0: outputs of the items in fragments/pass5.json.
outputs:P53A: Pass 5.3 Lane A: outputs of docker_container_run (fragments/pass53-A.json).
outputs:Z: Lane Z (merge/contract) owns no items. It carries cross-lane questions raised while merging lanes A-E; per-lane questions stay in each lane's file.

Lane Z fix: removed schema=compose-go-embedded from the 7 build.shm_size fields in C.json (Lane C reported it as a generator mistake). build.shm_size is integer|string in both compose-spec.json and compose-go-embedded.json (#/$defs/workload_spec/properties/build/oneOf/1/properties/shm_size); only container_spec.shm_size differs.

Decided by the user 2026-11-08 (Pass 4.5 Lane Z), applied to A-E by Lane Z; the four cross-lane questions and the lane questions they answer (B: logs name, service/task inspect sensitivity; C: compose logs output; D: whole-Dockerfile sensitivity; E: buildkit_version, docker_cli_version) are closed.

Logs (Pass 4.5 Lane Z corrections): every logs item (engine:container-logs, swarm:service-logs, swarm:task-logs, compose:cli-logs) has raw `logs` (text, one line per entry: "<timestamp> <stream> <source> <message>") hashed as `content_sha256`, and structured `log_entries` list(object({timestamp, stream, source, message})); stream is stdout|stderr, or combined for a TTY; only message is sensitive. logs_json is gone. Each records `inputs` tail (default 1000) and since; rule L1.

Sixth category `result`: the outcome of running an action or a descriptive value about how data was produced, not the identity or state of a lasting object. Every structured output of an action is now `result` (prune results, container state after start/stop/..., exec/wait/run results, service update_status/update_response/mode/service_status, node spec, swarm tls_info/swarm_info/join_tokens, buildx bake/metadata/status/result); plus root_rotation_in_progress, force_update, image created, dockerfile reconstructed/fidelity, stack service_status. Identity handoff values (deleted IDs, tokens, digests) stay identity. V2 still asks resources and data sources for a structured output; V4 also applies to object-typed result outputs.

Sensitivity is per field (new rule V5): a structured or result output is sensitive as a whole only with a `sensitive_reason` (only the three join_tokens outputs, where every field is a secret). Otherwise the output is not sensitive and the secret-carrying FIELDs carry `sensitive: true`. Raw outputs (JSON/text strings) stay sensitive as before; hashes never are. Secret channels marked: container/service/task env, plugin settings/config env, image config env, volume driver options (CIFS/NFS passwords), compose environment/env_file/secrets/build args/ssh/secrets/dockerfile_inline/configs content/environment-sourced values, Dockerfile ENV values/ARG defaults/history created_by, build provenance, attestation statements, buildx driver_opts, bake args/secret/ssh/dockerfile_inline, log lines, exec/run stdout/stderr, registry identity_token. A `dynamic` field cannot hide nested values, so the whole field is marked (stack service spec, image config blobs, provenance).

Sensitivity judgment calls by Lane Z, reversible: (1) command lines (container args/cmd/entrypoint, service Args/Command, compose ps Command, compose top processes) are NOT a secret channel, following Lane A and CONTRACT.md's list; B and C had treated them as sensitive, so compose:cli-ps containers and compose:cli-top processes are now plain. (2) Lane C's parent-level marks on the whole `secrets` and `configs` maps were dropped (they hid every field); their environment/content children stay marked. (3) compose networks/models slices carry no secret channel and are now plain. Accepted risk: a secret interpolated (${VAR}) into a field that is not a secret channel is no longer hidden in plans; secrets belong in environment/secrets.

Version names (Pass 4.5 Lane Z corrections): V3 reads the registry in SCHEMA.md. docker_cli_version is registered but only allowed on items with uses_cli true; every item now carries uses_cli, and all are false (the provider never runs the docker CLI), so docker_cli_version was removed from stack, stacks, stack-services, manifest-list and manifest-inspect.

Result (Pass 4.5 Lane Z corrections): rule V6, every action has a result output. 26 actions had none and got one: archive_size (exports, image save/load), path_stat (upload, cp), changes (commits), image / built_images (build, import), enabled (plugin create), push_status / pull_status (plugin push, compose push/pull), autolock_managers (rotate unlock key), removed_counts (compose down), layers (compose publish), container_states (compose kill/pause/restart/scale/start/stop/unpause/up).
